content.value_statement: Modern product teams need consistent, polished UI guidance. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Apple-inspired rules for typography, color, spacing, components, motion, and UX review.
actual_capabilities: Provides typography hierarchy using Apple system font stack and SF Pro style guidance.
Defines light and dark color variables with neutral backgrounds and accent color.
Recommends a spacing rhythm from 4px to 96px for layout hierarchy.
Gives CSS examples for cards, primary buttons, hover states, and subtle animations.
Supplies a UX checklist for touch targets, contrast, width, spacing, dark mode, and motion.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, generated assets, or a component library.
Does not verify compliance with official Apple Human Interface Guidelines.
Does not test accessibility or performance automatically.
Does not provide full application architecture or framework-specific implementation.

use_cases.title: Polish Frontend Screens
use_cases.description: Apply consistent typography, spacing, cards, buttons, and motion to existing product screens.

use_cases.title: Review Product Flows
use_cases.description: Check hierarchy, progressive disclosure, contrast, touch targets, and primary action clarity before handoff.

use_cases.title: Prototype Premium Interfaces
use_cases.description: Create quick interface direction for landing pages, dashboards, and app screens with a restrained Apple-inspired style.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Apple Styling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the apple-ui-design skill to improve this screen with clean typography, balanced spacing, and one primary action. Keep the layout simple and explain the key changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Design Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the apple-ui-design skill to define typography, color, spacing, card, button, and motion tokens for a responsive web app. Include light and dark modes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Product Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the apple-ui-design skill to audit this multi-step workflow for clarity, hierarchy, touch targets, contrast, motion, and progressive disclosure. Prioritize issues by user impact.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Component System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the apple-ui-design skill to design a premium dashboard interface. Provide guidance for navigation, cards, primary actions, forms, empty states, and responsive behavior.

output_examples.input: Polish a checkout screen that feels cluttered and has three competing action buttons.
output_examples.output: A simplified hierarchy with one primary checkout action, quieter secondary links, larger touch targets, and clearer spacing between payment sections.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard for Apple-inspired visual quality and usability.
output: Use a stronger title hierarchy for the main metric area.
Reduce card shadows and rely on spacing for separation.
Keep animation subtle and tied to state changes.
Verify dark mode contrast before release.

output_examples.input: Create visual direction for a new mobile settings screen.
output_examples.output: A grouped settings layout with clear section titles, comfortable row spacing, system typography, restrained color, and direct feedback for toggles.

best_practices: Start with content hierarchy and one clear primary action before styling components.
Use the spacing scale consistently across layout, cards, and control groups.
Check touch targets, contrast, dark mode, and animation timing before release.
anti_patterns: Combining multiple competing primary actions on the same screen.
Using decorative fonts, heavy shadows, or oversized rounded cards without purpose.
Applying motion that distracts from user feedback or reduces performance.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps create clean, minimal, Apple-inspired interfaces for web and app screens.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: No. It contains design guidance, CSS examples, UX rules, and review checklists.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is this an official Apple design resource?
faq.answer: No. It is a community skill with Apple-inspired guidance, not official Apple documentation.

faq.question: Does it generate visual assets?
faq.answer: No. It guides layout, styling, and review decisions but does not provide image assets.

faq.question: How should I use it during UI review?
faq.answer: Ask it to check hierarchy, spacing, contrast, touch targets, motion, and primary action clarity.
